reason: The hypothesis combines the established effect of grain boundary density on oxidation kinetics (P13, P5) with the layered, selective oxidation mechanism observed in equiatomic HEAs (P3, P6, P9) and applies this dual mechanism to a new, non-equiatomic AM alloy (Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3) under both oxidizing and reducing conditions, proposing that AM-induced high boundary density specifically causes nonuniform, spallation-prone scales. This synthesis of microstructural and chemical mechanisms from separate sources into a single, testable framework for a new alloy and environment goes beyond any single passage.
